intro: These articles are for shops that make their own photos for a product page, and their own short ads. A ready-made ad brings an opening line, the words to say, a voice, and a person on screen. You add your product, then post the file on TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, or YouTube Shorts.

Read the article that matches the job, then open the tool it names. You can paste a [product link](page:url-to-video), pick an on-screen person from the [actor library](page:ai-actors), or start from a ready-made layout in the [template gallery](page:templates). There is no free plan. Downloads have no watermark, which means no extra mark is added on the file, and [plans start at $24.50 a month](page:pricing).

faq.q: What is an ad template in these articles?
faq.a: A ready-made ad with an opening line, the words to say, a voice, and a person on screen. You add your product instead of filming someone or building the ad from nothing.

faq.q: How does a template become a file?
faq.a: Upload a photo of your product, or paste the product page link. Type the sentence you want spoken. The tool gives you a clip that looks like a creator filmed it, and you can post that clip.

You can try another opening line, another person on screen, or another sentence without waiting for a film day. A creator can still film your main product. These files are the versions you try in an ad test.
Shops, marketers, and agencies that sell online. The articles cover a product photo, a short ad, a launch clip, a check before you publish, and someone wearing the item.
Yes. Upload one photo and follow the article into the tool it names. You do not need to edit the video yourself before the first file.

faq.q: Which kinds of products do the articles cover?
faq.a: They point at [beauty](page:ind-beauty-skincare), [fashion](page:ind-fashion-clothing), [food and drinks](page:ind-food-drinks), [home](page:ind-home-living), and [electronics](page:ind-electronics). The same tools work for other products you ship.

faq.q: Can I upload my own photo or a product page?
faq.a: Yes. A clear photo of the product you ship is the right start. You can also paste a product page link when the article names that tool.

faq.q: Which platforms can I post to?
faq.a: Post on [TikTok](page:plat-tiktok), [Instagram](page:plat-instagram), [Facebook](page:plat-facebook), [YouTube Shorts](page:plat-youtube-shorts), [Amazon](page:plat-amazon), or [Shopify](page:plat-shopify). A video can be tall (9:16), square (1:1), wide (16:9), 4:3, or 3:4. Product photos come out square.
No. Plans start at $24.50 a month with 200 credits. Credits pay for each photo or video. A download has no watermark. You see the cost before every job.

faq.q: Can I use the file in a paid ad?
faq.a: Yes. You can use a finished photo or clip in ads and on your store. It has no watermark. Do not say the person on screen is a real buyer. The [Content Policy](/content) says what you can upload.
The opening line and the layout are already there, so you spend the time on your product and your sentence. You are not building every ad from nothing.

faq.q: How much does a photo or a clip cost?
faq.a: A product photo is 24 credits. A 6-second clip is 24, 10 seconds is 40, 15 is 60, and 30 is 120. If a job fails, those credits come back.

faq.q: Are the people in the clips real customers?
faq.a: No. The person is made by the tool. Do not give them a name or a line that says they bought the product.
